title: William Wilberforce's birth chart
metaDescription: William Wilberforce's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 0.9° Virgo. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Tightest of all, Venus holds a square to Mars at 0.8° — close enough to weld taste to drive. A square is the tradition’s engine room: two drives at cross purposes, and the friction is the horsepower.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At the noon reference the Sun sits 0.9° into Virgo — the first decan, which the old scheme hands to Mercury. Same sign, different decan, different chart.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: Mercury holds 28.1° Virgo, Venus holds 16.9° Libra, Mars holds 16.0° Cancer — in the old shorthand, thought with its feet on the ground; attraction that begins as conversation; effort that surges when it matters.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The day's firmest angle joins Jupiter and Saturn — a sextile holding at 0.7°. The scheme reads a sextile as a door left unlocked. Useful, and entirely dependent on someone walking through it. Behind it, Venus square Mars at 0.8°, and Venus sextile Neptune at 1.0° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. The unknown hour cannot unmake any of this: every aspect named survived all twenty-five samples of the day.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: Mars opposes Jupiter while both square Venus. Two squares braced against one opposition make a t-square — the chart’s working end, where pressure keeps finding the same outlet. The Sun makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The dignity table, which predates the outer planets and only ever spoke for seven, marks four placements here. Mercury in Virgo at 28.1° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Venus in Libra at 16.9° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Mars in Cancer at 16.0° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Jupiter in Capricorn at 13.0° is in fall. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Balance, counted honestly across the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: elements earth 4, fire 3, water 2, air 1; modalities mutable 5, cardinal 4, fixed 1. Earth weights a chart toward the material and the durable — what can be built, kept, and relied on. Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Pluto were retrograde — the backward drift a body appears to make as the Earth overtakes it, read in the scheme as a function that reviews before it releases.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Virgo for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 12.2° between midnight and midnight. Fast enough that its degree is approximate, slow enough that its sign is not in doubt. At the noon reference it stands at 21.5°.
